Mughal Emperor Jahangir permitted the English East India Company to establish their factory in India [d4][d7]. Specifically, Jahangir granted a Farman to Captain William Hawkins, permitting the English to erect a factory at Surat in 1613 [d4]. In 1615, Thomas Roe, the Ambassador to James I, obtained an imperial Farman from Jahangir for trading and establishing factories across the Mughal Empire [d4]. Additionally, following the Anglo-Mughal War, Emperor Aurangzeb later allowed the Company to establish a presence on the eastern coast of India as well [d3], while Britannica notes that the Company "initially established itself in India by obtaining permission from local" authorities [d5].
